source_text: Haeretici nuptias auferunt, Psychici ingerunt. Illi nec semel, isti non semel nubunt. Quid agis, lex Creatoris? Inter alienos spadones et aurigas tuos tantumdem quereris de domestico obsequio, quantum de fastidio extraneo; proinde et te laedunt qui abutuntur, quemadmodum qui non utuntur. Verum neque continentia ejusmodi laudanda, quia haeretica est; neque licentia defendenda, quia psychica est. Illa blasphemat, ista luxuriat. Illa destruit nuptiarum Deum, ista confundit. Penes nos autem, quos spirituales merito dici facit agnitio spiritalium charismatum, continentia tam religiosa est, quam licentia verecunda, quandoquidem ambae cum Creatore sunt. Continentia legem nuptiarum honorat, licentia temperat. Illa non cogitur; ista regitur. Illa arbitrium habet, haec modum. Unum matrimonium novimus, sicut unum Deum. Magis honorem refert lex nuptiarum, ubi habet et pudorem. Sed Psychicis non recipientibus spiritum, ea quae sunt spiritus non placent. Ita, dum quae sunt spiritus non placent, ea quae sunt carnis placebunt, ut contraria spiritui. Caro, inquit, adversus spiritum concupiscit, et spiritus adversus carnem. Quid autem concupiscet caro, quam quae magis carnis sunt? Propter quod et in primordio extranea spiritus facta est: Non, inquit, permanebit spiritus meus in istis hominibus in aevum, eo quod caro sint.
pass_a_gloss: Heretics take away marriages, Psychics introduce them. Those do not marry even once, these do not marry only once. What are you doing, law of the Creator? You complain about domestic obedience as much as about foreign disdain, and therefore both those who abuse and those who do not use it hurt you. Truly, neither this kind of self-control is to be praised, because it is heretical, nor is license to be defended, because it is psychic. The former blasphemes, the latter indulges in luxury. The former destroys the God of marriages, the latter confuses. However, among us, who are rightly called spiritual due to the recognition of spiritual gifts, self-control is as religious as license is modest, since both are with the Creator. Self-control honors the law of marriage, license moderates it. The former is not forced, the latter is governed. The former has judgment, the latter has moderation. We know one marriage, just as we know one God. The law of marriage brings more honor where it also has shame. But to the Psychics, who do not receive the Spirit, the things that are of the Spirit are not pleasing. Thus, while the things that are of the Spirit are not pleasing, the things that are of the flesh will be pleasing, as opposed to the Spirit. The flesh, it says, desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. What, then, will the flesh desire, except what is more of the flesh? Because of which, the flesh was also made foreign to the Spirit from the beginning: 'My Spirit', it says, 'will not remain in these men forever, because they are flesh'.

pass_b_english: Heretics abolish marriage; Psychics multiply it. The former refuse to marry even once, the latter refuse to stop at once. What are you doing, law of the Creator? You complain about domestic obedience just as much as foreign contempt, so both those who abuse marriage and those who refuse it wound you alike. Truly, such continence deserves no praise because it is heretical, and such license deserves no defense because it is psychic. The one blasphemes; the other wallows in lust. The one destroys the God of marriage; the other confuses him. But among us—who are rightly called spiritual because we acknowledge spiritual gifts—continence is as devout as license is modest, since both stand with the Creator. Continence honors the law of marriage; license moderates it. The former is not forced; the latter is governed. The former exercises judgment; the latter observes measure. We know one marriage, just as we know one God. The law of marriage gains greater honor where it also has shame. Yet Psychics, because they do not receive the Spirit, find no pleasure in the things of the Spirit. So while the things of the Spirit displease them, the things of the flesh will please them, as contrary to the Spirit. "The flesh," it says, "desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh" (Gal 5:17). What, then, will the flesh desire except what is more fleshly? Because of this, the flesh was also made alien to the Spirit from the beginning: "My Spirit," it says, "will not remain in these men forever, because they are flesh" (Gen 6:3).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the distinctions between the Heretical and Psychic views. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the necessary scripture citations (Gal 5:17) and (Gen 6:3) which were alluded to in the Latin text, fulfilling the requirement for added identifications. Pass A and B are consistent with the Locked Latin.
